title: Cervical pessary in pregnancy
what: The doctor places a soft silicone ring in the vagina. It supports the cervix and helps keep the pregnancy going.
why: When the cervix gets shorter or opens too early, with a risk of preterm birth.
duration: placing it usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; it is usually worn until 36 to 37 weeks
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are
If you have discharge, itching, or bleeding
If you had a preterm birth before

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A swab is usually taken first to make sure there is no infection.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Use the toilet before it is placed.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes and socks, and bring a pad.

steps: You lie on the exam chair
The doctor looks at the cervix with a speculum
The ring is coated with gel
It is gently put in and placed around the cervix
The doctor checks how it sits
Sometimes an ultrasound is done right away
feel: While it is placed, you feel pressure and some discomfort
Afterward, you usually barely feel it
You may have a little more discharge
after: Come to your checkups as scheduled. The doctor will check the ring and the cervix
Sex is usually not recommended. Ask your doctor
Sometimes suppositories or swabs are prescribed to prevent infection
The ring is removed at the clinic, usually close to your due date
red_flags: Contractions or pain low in your belly: call your doctor or emergency services
The ring fell out or bothers you a lot

faq.a: It usually does not hurt, but it is unpleasant. It takes a few minutes.

faq.q: Can I walk and work with a pessary?
faq.a: Usually yes, with limits on physical effort. Your doctor will tell you what is allowed.

reminders.text: Pessary placement tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record and a pad.
